title: test: concurrent sign/verify thread-safety hammer test
description:
wolfP11 has never been tested under concurrent load. The sign/verify path involves per-session state (sign_active, verify_active, sign_key, verify_key) and global key table (g_keys). These must be safe under concurrent access.

Write a test in test/wp11_test_pkcs11_threads.c:

Thread safety test 1 — N threads each doing independent sign cycles:
- N=8 threads, each opens its own session, generates its own key, loops 1000x: C_SignInit → C_Sign → verify with wc_ecc_verify_hash
- Success criterion: all signatures verify correctly; no CKR_FUNCTION_FAILED or CKR_GENERAL_ERROR; no crashes
- Detects: g_keys[] read/write races, sign_active corruption across sessions

Thread safety test 2 — concurrent sign + session open/close:
- Thread A: loops C_OpenSession → C_Login → 100x (C_SignInit → C_Sign) → C_CloseSession
- Thread B: simultaneously loops C_OpenSession → C_CloseSession on the same slot
- Success criterion: no crash, no session handle returned twice, all sign ops succeed or return valid error (not garbage)
- Detects: session slot allocation races

Thread safety test 3 — sign vs. FindObjects interleave:
- Thread A: tight loop C_SignInit → C_Sign
- Thread B: tight loop C_FindObjectsInit → C_FindObjects → C_FindObjectsFinal
- Success criterion: no crash, sign results cryptographically correct
- Detects: g_keys[] iteration races

Run under valgrind --tool=helgrind and/or ThreadSanitizer (-fsanitize=thread) to catch races that don't manifest as crashes.

Guard with #ifdef WOLFP11_CFG_TEST_THREADS and add to Makefile as a separate test target.
